feature: Copy takes the layer you picked
summary: Pick a layer, drag a marquee over part of it and press ⌘C: you now get that layer's pixels inside the marquee, trimmed to what is drawn there, instead of every layer flattened together. Everything flattened together moved to ⇧⌘C as Edit ▸ Copy Merged, and ⌘X follows copy.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. The flag Copy takes the layer you picked is on by default in the Experiments window. Open any picture and draw a shape on top of it so the document has two layers.

try.do: Pick the shape you drew, in the layers list or on the picture.
Take the marquee, the dashed square second along the tool bar, and drag a box across the shape's corner, carrying on over the picture behind it.
Read the new row's W and H in Position & Size: it is the corner of the shape alone, with none of the picture behind it.
Press ⌘Z, drag the same marquee again, and this time press ⇧⌘C then ⌘V.
Open the Edit menu and read Copy and Copy Merged one under the other.
Copy the shape's corner again and paste it into another app, a chat or a note, to see the picture land there.
Pick the picture layer UNDER the shape, marquee the same spot and press ⌘X: the piece comes out of the picture and the shape above it is untouched.

evaluate: With a layer picked and a marquee up, is the layer's own pixels what you expected ⌘C to give you?

A copy is trimmed to the pixels that are actually there, so a marquee flung round a small drawing hands back the drawing rather than a big transparent box. Is that right, or do you want the copy to be the size of the marquee you drew?
Nothing on screen says which of the two copies you just took. Do you want a word at the bottom of the canvas saying what landed, or is silence right for a key you press all day?
A marquee that misses the picked layer copies nothing and beeps. Is a beep enough, or should it say why?
Copy Merged moved out of the File menu, where it was called Copy Image, into Edit under Copy. Is that where you would look for it?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every shot above is a real capture of the probe window, not an offscreen render.

What was driven, with the probe: a two layer picture, a marquee across the top layer's corner, ⌘C and ⌘V, the same marquee with ⇧⌘C and ⌘V, no marquee at all, the layer UNDER another one, a marquee that misses, and cut. Saved as Scripts/playtest/copy-takes-your-layer-walk.json so it stays a regression check.

Pasting into another app was checked by a separate process reading the clipboard the way a pasting app does: it got a 200 by 150 picture of the shape's corner and nothing else. It was not pasted into a named app by hand, because this loop is not allowed to drive other apps on your machine.

With nothing picked and a marquee up, ⌘C still takes every layer flattened together. That is deliberate: with no layer to prefer there is nothing else it could mean, and it keeps ⌘A ⌘C ⌘V duplicating what you see.

Cut on a SHAPE or a piece of text with a marquee up still takes the whole layer, because slicing a corner off a shape would mean turning it into pixels first and that is not something ⌘X should decide. Only a picture layer is sliced. Filed as its own task.
New Layer via Copy (⌘J) still promotes the flattened picture rather than the layer you picked, so it now disagrees with ⌘C. Filed as its own task.
Not built: the copy says nothing on screen either way. The notice pill exists and could carry it, but a pill on every ⌘C could be noise, so it is a question above rather than a guess.
